program_name: Management (Laurea Magistrale / second-cycle degree) — International Business curriculum (the English-taught 'International Business' track within the Management LM; distinct from the other English-taught curriculum 'Green Economy and Sustainability' and from the Italian-taught curricula of the same degree)
teaching_language: English for this curriculum. The International Business curriculum is delivered entirely in English (2 years, 120 ECTS). The parent Management LM as a whole is bilingual at programme level: it offers two English-taught curricula (International Business; Green Economy and Sustainability) alongside Italian-taught curricula (Business finance; Marketing; Logistics and production). Students choose the English or the Italian articulation.
campus: Brescia. Department of Economics and Management (DEM), Via San Faustino 74/B, Brescia. Part of the second year may be spent abroad under the double-degree agreements (Hochschule Mainz, Germany; Nottingham Business School / Nottingham Trent University, UK). [uncertain]
degree_class: LM-77 — Scienze economico-aziendali (Economics and Business Administration). The class applies to the whole Management LM, including the International Business curriculum. [uncertain]
english_delivery_scope: english_curriculum_within_italian_programme. The Management LM is a single Italian degree (class LM-77) containing several curricula; only two of them — International Business and Green Economy and Sustainability — are taught in English, while Business finance, Marketing and Logistics and production are taught in Italian. This record covers ONLY the International Business curriculum, whose courses are entirely in English. A candidate is admitted to the Management LM and then follows the English-language articulation, so the degree title on the diploma is the Management LM with the International Business curriculum, not a separate English-only degree.
programme_status: active_first_year. The Management LM and its International Business curriculum are admitting new first-year students; the enrolling page publishes admission-test dates for a.y. 2026/2027 (1 July 2026 and 24 September 2026) and a pre-evaluation of curricular requirements form dated April 2026 for a.y. 2026/2027. Not phasing out, not under accreditation.
pre_evaluation_required: Two distinct pre-evaluation mechanisms apply. (a) Domestic/curricular pre-evaluation: UNIBS publishes a 'prevalutazione dei requisiti curriculari per l'accesso' form for the Management LM (Req_Min_MANAG, a.y. 2026/2027) which candidates use to have their curricular credits checked in advance; the MIB flyer describes an online pre-evaluation procedure opening in December. (b) International pre-evaluation for foreign-qualification holders: compulsory via the PICA online platform. For open-access master's degrees in the Economics, Engineering and Law areas — which includes the Management LM — pre-evaluation by the relevant Commission is compulsory for candidates with foreign degrees, to verify curricular and personal-preparation requirements. A EUR 20 fee is charged at the end of the PICA procedure. Rounds: a first round reserved to non-EU citizens living abroad (also the round for the LMINT and STAR PVS international scholarships), closing 15 March 2026 at noon Italian time, plus later rounds for EU and EU-equivalent citizens with foreign degrees (pre-evaluation only, no scholarship; in the previous cycle 30 June - 21 July at noon Italian time). [uncertain]
entry_test_name: There is no external standardised entry test mandated for this programme (no TOLC, no SAT, no CISIA test). The internal instrument is the UNIBS Economics-area 'admission test' (test di ammissione / verifica della preparazione personale) for the Management LM, administered by the university itself. Notably, the GMAT (Graduate Management Admission Test, GMAC) is accepted as an alternative exemption route: a GMAT score of at least 600/800 exempts the candidate from the internal admission test. The internal test is a pass/fail eligibility check, not a ranked selective competition — the programme is open access with no numerus clausus. [uncertain]
admission_type: Open access (accesso libero) with compulsory verification of minimum curricular requirements and of personal preparation; no numerus clausus. Candidates who do not qualify for direct admission must sit an internal admission test. Foreign-qualification holders must additionally pass the compulsory PICA pre-evaluation.
academic_requirements: Candidates must hold a bachelor's degree (laurea) or a university diploma of at least three years' duration, or an equivalent foreign qualification, with demonstrated preparation in accounting and management, economics, mathematics and statistics, and law. CURRICULAR REQUIREMENTS: a minimum of 55 CFU in total, distributed across five groups of scientific-disciplinary sectors (SSD) — business/management, economics, quantitative (mathematics-statistics), legal, and language. Within the business/management area (ambito economico-aziendale) at least 21 CFU must have been obtained in one or more of the sectors SECS-P/07, SECS-P/08, SECS-P/09, SECS-P/10, SECS-P/11 or ING-IND/35 (industrial/managerial engineering sector as listed on the UNIBS form). PERSONAL PREPARATION: satisfying the personal-preparation requirement gives direct admission and exemption from the admission test. It is granted to candidates with a weighted average of examination marks of at least 23/30, or who have passed the GMAT with a score of at least 600/800. For candidates holding a degree obtained abroad, a Commission verifies both the curricular requirements and the personal preparation; personal preparation is deemed achieved if the bachelor's degree final mark is at least 85/110 (equivalently 77/100). The International Business curriculum specifically advertises a minimum overall undergraduate grade / CGPA of 77/100 together with CEFR B2 English. Candidates who satisfy neither the 23/30 average nor the GMAT threshold must sit and pass the admission test.
language_requirements: CEFR level B2 in English is required for the English-taught curricula, including International Business. Accepted evidence, as alternatives: an official B2 (or higher) English certificate; having completed the previous degree course in an English-taught programme; having passed English-language examinations in the previous university career for at least 3 CFU; or having acquired at least 60 CFU in activities delivered in English. There is a documented conflict in the sources: the UNIBS PDF 'Requisiti corsi di laurea magistrale in lingua Inglese' (December 2024 version) appears in one indexed snippet to state B1 CEFR and a minimum final grade of 73/100 for a Management-related entry, whereas the Management International Business flyer and the Management enrolling page state B2 and 77/100. The B2 + 77/100 combination is the one consistently attached to the International Business curriculum, but this must be confirmed on the live pages. Note also that for some UNIBS master's programmes candidates holding only B1 may be admitted with a study plan containing 3 additional CFU of language work to reach B2 before graduation — whether this concession extends to the Management International Business curriculum is unverified. [uncertain]
application_deadline_eu: For Italian and EU/EU-equivalent candidates, enrolment follows the annual Economics-area master's degree notice (Avviso LM Economia). The two published admission-test sittings for a.y. 2026/2027 are 1 July 2026 at 10:30 (first edition) and 24 September 2026 at 10:30 (second edition), and a positive result is valid for admission to a.y. 2026/2027 — the application to sit each test must be filed before the respective sitting. Direct online admission/enrolment applications are accepted up to 31 December of the academic year concerned (late/'in-year' enrolment window). EU citizens holding a foreign qualification must in addition use the PICA pre-evaluation round for EU candidates (previous cycle: 30 June - 21 July at noon Italian time). Exact 2026/2027 dates must be read from the current Avviso. [uncertain]
application_deadline_non_eu: Non-EU candidates residing abroad: PICA pre-evaluation first round for a.y. 2026/2027 closes 15 March 2026 at noon (Italian time), which is also the round used for the LMINT and STAR PVS international scholarships. After a positive pre-evaluation, non-EU candidates living abroad must submit and complete the pre-enrolment / study-visa request on the Universitaly portal by 31 August 2026, then matriculate at UNIBS after visa issuance. The Universitaly/visa deadline is a separate step from the UNIBS PICA pre-evaluation deadline and must not be conflated with it. Non-EU candidates already legally resident in Italy follow the distinct 'Non-EU candidates living in Italy: master's degrees' procedure and do not use Universitaly. The MIB flyer additionally refers to an online pre-evaluation opening in December for the International Business curriculum. [uncertain]
required_documents: For PICA pre-evaluation and subsequent enrolment, foreign-qualification candidates must provide: the degree diploma and the transcript of records in the original language with an official translation into Italian or English (unless already issued in one of these languages), legalised or bearing the Apostille stamp issued by the authorities of the relevant education system; the Declaration of Value (Dichiarazione di valore in loco) from the competent Italian diplomatic representation, or an equivalent CIMEA statement of comparability where accepted; detailed syllabi/programmes of the examinations taken, stamped by the foreign university and translated into Italian or English (a preferential requirement); proof of English at CEFR B2 (certificate, or transcript evidence of at least 3 CFU of English or of a degree with at least 60 CFU taught in English); a GMAT score report if the candidate uses the GMAT 600/800 exemption route; a valid passport/identity document; and payment of the EUR 20 pre-evaluation fee. Italian-degree candidates submit degree and transcript data through the university online enrolment system and, where relevant, the Req_Min_MANAG curricular-requirements pre-evaluation form. [uncertain]
entry_exam_or_test: Admission requires possession of the minimum curricular requirements plus adequate personal preparation. Personal preparation requirements allow direct admission to the course of study and consequent exemption from the admission test: they are granted to candidates with a weighted average of examinations of no less than 23/30, or who have passed the GMAT with a score of no less than 600/800. Candidates who do not meet either condition must sit the internal admission test, held for a.y. 2026/2027 on 1 July 2026 at 10:30 (first edition) and 24 September 2026 at 10:30 (second edition); a positive result is valid for admission to a.y. 2026/2027. For candidates holding a degree obtained abroad, a Commission verifies the curricular requirements and the personal preparation, the latter deemed achieved with a bachelor's degree mark of at least 85/110 (or 77/100). For the English-taught International Business curriculum the assessment is combined with the B2 English requirement; a separate interview may be arranged where the documentary evidence is insufficient. The exact format (written multiple-choice vs interview) of the Management LM admission test was not directly verifiable. [uncertain]

uncertainty_notes: MAJOR ACCESS CAVEAT: unibs.it and corsi.unibs.it are behind an AWS WAF / Cloudflare-style 'managed challenge' (Human Verification). Every direct access attempt failed: WebFetch on https://corsi.unibs.it/en/management and https://corsi.unibs.it/en/management/enrolling returned HTTP 405; https://www.unibs.it/en/cds-datascience and the official PDFs (flyer_DEF_MIB.pdf, Requisiti corsi di laurea magistrale in lingua Inglese.pdf, Req_Min_MANAG.pdf) returned HTTP 403/405; curl with a full desktop browser User-Agent returned the AWS WAF 'Human Verification' interstitial; the browser tool loaded only the 'Let's confirm you are human' security check, and solving that challenge is not permitted. Therefore NO page or PDF was directly verified: the whole record was compiled from search-engine indexed content and cached snippets of the official corsi.unibs.it and www.unibs.it pages, and all source_quotes are reconstructed from those indexed snippets rather than read from the live page — wording may differ from the live text and every value should be re-verified before publication. SPECIFIC UNCERTAINTIES AND CONFLICTS: (1) CONFLICT ON GRADE AND ENGLISH LEVEL — one indexed snippet of the UNIBS PDF 'Requisiti corsi di laurea magistrale in lingua Inglese' (December 2024) reports a minimum final grade of 73/100 and CEFR B1 for a Management-related entry, while the MIB flyer and the Management enrolling page report 77/100 and CEFR B2. It is unclear whether the 73/100 + B1 figures belong to a different English-taught programme listed in the same PDF, to the Green Economy and Sustainability curriculum, or to an earlier version of the requirements. Resolve on the live page before relying on either. (2) CURRICULUM-LEVEL SEPARATION — the admission thresholds recorded here (55 CFU total, 21 CFU in SECS-P/07-11 or ING-IND/35, 23/30 weighted average or GMAT 600, 85/110 or 77/100 for foreign degrees) come from Management-LM-wide sources; it could not be verified from the indexed snippets whether the International Business curriculum applies any ADDITIONAL or DIFFERENT threshold compared with the Green Economy and Sustainability curriculum. The only requirement clearly and specifically attached to the International Business curriculum in the sources is the 77/100 + B2 combination on the MIB flyer. (3) The sixth SSD in the business/management group is reported as ING-IND/35 here; an indexed snippet rendered it as 'ING-IND/16', which is a manufacturing-technology sector and would be unusual in a management-credits list — the correct code must be confirmed on Req_Min_MANAG.pdf. (4) degree_class LM-77 comes from the Italian UNIBS programme page snippet and AlmaLaurea transparency data, not from the English corsi.unibs.it page. (5) campus/address (Via San Faustino 74/B) is from an indexed snippet of a sibling DEM programme page and was not confirmed for this specific programme. (6) The list of Italian-taught curricula (Business finance; Marketing; Logistics and production) is from an indexed snippet and the exact curriculum names may differ. (7) Deadlines: the 31 December enrolment date is the in-year/conditional enrolment limit from the Economics-area notice, not necessarily the ordinary enrolment deadline; the EU PICA round dates (30 June - 21 July) are from the previous cycle; the flyer's 'online pre-evaluation in December' may refer to an International-Business-specific early round distinct from the PICA international rounds, and this distinction is unresolved. (8) required_documents — the CIMEA statement-of-comparability alternative is general Italian practice and was not explicitly confirmed on UNIBS pages. (9) The format of the Management admission test (written vs oral) and its syllabus were not verifiable. (10) Precise tuition amounts for the International Business curriculum were not captured; only the fee landing pages are given. (11) Double-degree details: Nottingham Trent (second semester of second year at Nottingham Business School) is documented; the Hochschule Mainz double-degree structure and its selection criteria for the International Business curriculum were not verified.
